text: Disputed: whether the round-3 review still has a C list to answer, after the lane held worker/T-0317 BACK 'kind=review' three times running. Checked directly: none of the three reviews (1/2/3-t-0317.md) has a `## C` heading or any C-list content — `asf.evidence.review.c_items()` returns `[]` for all three, and each says in prose "No C list — nothing found that blocks." The hold is a false positive of the lane's own tooling: `asf.reviews.verdict()` (asf/reviews.py:150-158) derives BOUNCE (read as CHANGES by asf/evidence/review.py) because its `missing()` check requires an exact normalized-string match between the table's row names and `CHECKLIST['code']`'s literal text, and the rows all three reviewers wrote ("scope: the diff stays inside `writes:`", "acceptance tests byte-identical to the plan's") are exactly what `asf/briefs/templates/review.md:10-15` itself instructs every reviewer to write — a drift between the checklist (added by T-0265/#135) and the template that was never reconciled. Rounds 1-2 additionally hit a hard table-parse fault from an unescaped `|` inside one evidence cell's grep pattern. This is not specific to T-0317: the same table wording bounces docs/reviews/1-b-0087.md, 1-b-0090.md, 1-b-0099.md and 1-b-0110.md identically. Overruled: there is no C list and no code defect — the diff, the tests, and the gate are exactly what three independent rounds each verified and approved; T-0317's footprint and content stand unchanged. Separately, round 2's carried-forward I-item (write_agents_file's `tools=()` rendering `"tools": []`, spec §2.1 vs §2.4's worked example) is also not a Task-1 defect — T4's acceptance text (docs/specs/f-0062.md:746) literally reads "tools is the row's set minus deny_tools", and asf/roles/launch.py:144 implements that formula exactly — but it stays open, unresolved, for whoever wires Task 4/5's launch to confirm the rendered agents file is read the way the runtime expects.

Three prior sessions left `plan/F-0067` empty — no `docs/plans/f-0067.md`, no `docs/reviews/1-f-0067.md`, no Task cards anywhere in the repo's history. This was a starved plan, not a content dispute: there were no two readings to weigh, only nothing committed after three attempts. I read the approved spec in full and verified every precondition its §1.1 states against this checkout (`step_health.run()`'s statement order, `worktrees.safety`'s two `unpushed commit(s)` exits, `retention.owned_patterns`, `doctor.run`'s row order, `groom`'s `EXTRA_SECTIONS`, `plugin_build`'s skill list) — all matched exactly, so the spec itself was never the obstacle. `docs/plans/f-0066.md` (landed since, at `eac200f76`) gave the precedent for how this factory plans a tightly-coupled single-new-module feature, and `T-0317`'s ruling (`111165f56`) gave the precedent for not forcing a split where one does not exist. So I wrote and landed the missing plan myself rather than ordering a fourth attempt: five Tasks — `conventions.py`'s `floor:` map (no dependency), the whole of `asf/floor.py` plus its two satellite files `retention.py`/`worktrees.py` (one Task: the registry, probes, sweep and hold branch all share one new file and one test module, and `CLASSES`' own `FloorError` check at import means a partial table fails its own registry test — it does not split), then three independent callers (doctor row, groom section, tick+CLI wiring) that each need only the leaf. Verified against the live parser: `plan_task_records`/`writes_lines`/`task_order` read the five headings, their `writes:` and `after:` lines exactly as intended (`{1: [], 2: [1], 3: [2], 4: [2], 5: [2]}`), so Task cards will mint correctly once this plan lands on `main`. One standing, already-repeatedly-recorded defect noted in the plan itself (PD8) and not fixed here, out of this Feature's footprint: `plan_tasks.STORY_ID_RE` is four digits and the spec's Story ids are five, so the minted Task cards' `stories:` field will read empty — the same defect a dozen other landed plans in this repo have already recorded at this head. Nothing else was in dispute; the card's own "fold into the clean-floor Feature?" question was already answered by the spec itself (§1.3: stands alone either way) and is not reopened.

All three rounds' C list held the same finding — Task 5 is undelivered (no `session.sh coder off`/`bare` session, no `grant-<n>` legs, no table, no P08 paragraph, no stamp) — and round 2/3 additionally recorded the cause: Task 5's own header (`docs/plans/f-0065.md:450`) declares `after: Task 4`, and Task 4 (`docs/plans/f-0065.md:361-384`, footprint `docs/research/sandboxed-worker-shell.md`) is the Task that creates that document — its stamp and §2.7 items 1-2 — so that Task 5 appends rather than creates. I verified both anchors directly: the file does not exist anywhere in the tree, and no commit touching it or naming Task 4 exists on any branch (`git log --all` for both). Both C-list items are upheld as true, but the fix is not a commit on `worker/T-0329` — no legitimate edit exists inside this Task's scope that doesn't mean fabricating Task 4's stamp/§2.7 items 1-2 or hand-writing rows the plan forbids (D12). The three rounds looped because the review kept asking for a correction where none is possible until the prerequisite lands. Ruling: T-0329 is blocked, not defective. It waits for Task 4 (backlog id T-0328, per the reviews' own search pattern and the T-0327→T-0328→T-0329 sequential numbering visible in this repo's commit history) to land `docs/research/sandboxed-worker-shell.md` with its stamp and §2.7 items 1-2 first. The one change already on the branch (`coder.grant-7.json`'s registry slot, `registry.npmjs.org`) is correct per all three reviews' "I" sections and should be kept when Task 5 resumes. This finding does not come back in a later round: the loop ends here, and the card should not be re-dispatched until T-0328's card is Done.

Three review rounds held the identical finding — Task 5 declares `after: Task 4` (`docs/plans/f-0065.md:450`), and Task 4 is the Task that creates `docs/research/sandboxed-worker-shell.md`, which Task 5 is meant to append a table into. I checked the claim directly: the file does not exist anywhere in the tree, no commit for it exists on any branch, and Task 4's minted id is `T-0328` (Task 3 landed as `T-0327` in the log, this card is Task 5 = `T-0329`, so Task 4 sits between them at `T-0328`, which has landed nowhere). The plan's own PD1 gives the reason this ordering is real rather than a formality: Task 4 answers the permission-mode question specifically so a bad answer stops the spike "before ten sessions are spent on rows the answer voids" — launching Task 5's coder-table sessions ahead of Task 4 is the exact waste the plan exists to prevent. The finding is upheld: this is a scheduling fact, not a defect in the branch, so nothing on `worker/T-0329` needs editing — the two prior "changes requested" correction rounds were asking for work that cannot start yet. The lone substantive change already on the branch (the `coder.grant-7.json` registry fix) is correct per all three reviews' `I` notes and should stay. This ruling ends the loop: T-0329 is not corrected again until T-0328 lands.

Round 3's C list is upheld in full, both bullets confirmed independently against the checkout rather than taken on the reviewer's word. Task 5 is genuinely undelivered — the branch carries only the single 2-line coder.grant-7.json fix plus the three review commits, none of the plan's six Steps at docs/plans/f-0065.md:447-503 exist, and the Gate's first command still returns rc=1. More decisively, Task 5 cannot be delivered from this branch at all: its Files section (docs/plans/f-0065.md:463-465) requires appending §2.7 item 3 to docs/research/sandboxed-worker-shell.md, a document Task 4 opens with the stamp and §2.7 items 1-2 (docs/plans/f-0065.md:361-381, "after: Task 3" — the document is "new" there). No commit anywhere in this repository's history touches that path, so Task 4 has never landed on any branch; Task 5's own plan line reads "after: Task 4" (docs/plans/f-0065.md:450). Three rounds of "changes requested" asked this session to do work that has no input to act on — a fourth correction round would repeat the same failure for the same reason. What changes: this item stops being treated as a correctable defect on worker/T-0329 and becomes a dependency wait. No commit was made because no edit inside this branch's writes: (tools/spike/f-0065/**, docs/research/sandboxed-worker-shell.md) can manufacture Task 4's missing output; the round-3 "I" note (coder.grant-7.json's registry fix) stands and needs no change. I could not confirm Task 4's card id from this worktree — per this record's own constraint, a worktree/adjudicate session cannot read backlog card files (only the groom/inbox dirs and the worktree are reachable), so the id→ordinal mapping (T-0329 is Task 5; Task 4 is very likely T-0328 by sequential minting, per PD2's mint-from-plan-ordinal rule) is a plausible but unverified guess, not a fact I'll assert. blocked_on should be set to whatever card the record shows for F-0065's Task 4 (the fence-proved-on / permission-mode-pair / environment-hole Task, docs/plans/f-0065.md:361); if the record confirms it is T-0328, use that id directly.

Round 1, 2 and 3's C list are the same finding restated, and both its bullets are upheld. Bullet 1 (Task 5's six Steps are all undone — no `off`/`bare` session, no `grant-<n>` leg, no table, no P08 paragraph, no stamp) is true but downstream of bullet 2, which is the real blocker: Task 5 declares `after: Task 4` (`docs/plans/f-0065.md:450`), and Task 4 — not Task 5 — is the Task that creates `docs/research/sandboxed-worker-shell.md` in the first place, writing §2.7's items 1-2 (`docs/plans/f-0065.md:363,375`). I confirmed against the checkout, not the review's word for it: `git log --all --oneline` shows T-0325, T-0326 and T-0327 (Tasks 1-3) landed on main, but no commit or branch for T-0328 (Task 4) exists anywhere in this repository, and `docs/research/sandboxed-worker-shell.md` is absent from every branch. Task 5 has no document to append a table to and cannot be delivered — three rounds of "changes requested" were asking for work that structurally cannot exist yet, which is why the same finding held three times: a fourth correction commit on `worker/T-0329` would fail the identical way. What changes: T-0329 is blocked on T-0328, not in need of more code. The one thing already on the branch — `coder.grant-7.json`'s registry-slot fix — is correct per both round 1 and round 3's `I` note and is kept as-is; it costs nothing to carry until Task 4 lands. This finding does not come back in a later round: any future review of T-0329 that reopens "Task 5 undelivered" without first checking whether T-0328 has landed is re-litigating a settled ruling.
